name: Library of Congress — Chronicling America
notes: Historic American newspapers through 1963; primary discovery backbone.

name: American Antiquarian Society — Newspapers
notes: Major early-American collection; more than 20,000 titles and two million issues.

name: Howard University — Black Press Archives
notes: More than 2,000 newspaper titles and over 100,000 individual issues.

name: Schomburg Center — Black Newspapers
notes: Representative Black newspaper holdings and broader Schomburg archival collections.

name: Freedom's Journal — Library of Congress
notes: First African American-owned and operated newspaper in the United States, founded 1827.

name: New York Post — Library of Congress record
notes: Established in 1801 by Alexander Hamilton as the New-York Evening Post.

name: Sequoyah National Research Center
notes: Extensive American Indian, Alaska Native and First Nations newspaper and periodical holdings.

name: Sequoyah — Indigenous Newspapers in North America
notes: Thousands of editions from Indigenous publications; some access is on-site/subscription.

name: California Digital Newspaper Collection
notes: Digitized California newspapers for Western and local reporting.

name: Hoji Shinbun Digital Collection
notes: Japanese diaspora newspapers; useful for Japanese American community press research.
